audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer rates the lane HARD 8/10 with Yasuo winning all 7 stages; content and packet give Mel all 7; WR is 48.46%. The two layers argue and neither blanket chart is credible.
audit.why: A near-even WR supports neither all-Mel nor all-Yasuo. I could not adjudicate per row from the kit alone, so the chart was left untouched and the question raised to the user.
Spike structure (E-root pattern 3-5, R-denial at 6, wall-bait at items) is sound once the wall-ignore claim is removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content claims Solar Snare 'ignores Wind Wall' / 'roots through the wall' in whys[2], whys[6], spikes[0], spikes[2], spikes[3], mid, late and wants.you[0].
audit.why: The kit flags Mel's E as a projectile ('can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects') and Riot's text says she 'fires a radiant orb forward'. Trusting the description, the wall-ignore claim is unsupported; rewrote those passages around baiting the 25s wall with the 10s Q instead.
audit.corrected: All wall-ignore language removed; the wall-bait pattern (25s W vs 10s Q, 4s uptime) stated with numbers.

audit.why: Kit: Wind Wall 25/23/21/19/17 with 4s uptime, Last Breath 70/50/30, Sweeping Blade 0.5s, Mel W 38-26.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Rebuttal like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1, 17s max, 4s uptime — every projectile you own waits on it; commit in the 20s gap. - His R is 70/50/30s; deny the knockup and it rots. - Guard your W Rebuttal (38s early) for the tornado. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: His Sweeping Blade is a 0.5s dash he chains through minions — drop Solar Snare on his path and the engage dies mid-hop.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Q3 loaded means the tornado knockup into Last Breath — sidestep first, volley second; a stationary Mel is his whole combo.

edits.before: Level 3 you lead because Solar Snare is a ground root that ignores Wind Wall and locks his dash.
edits.after: Level 3 you lead because Solar Snare roots his Sweeping Blade approach before he ever reaches you.

edits.before: First item keeps you ahead because he wastes Wind Wall on your Q and still eats an un-wallable E root.
edits.after: First item keeps you ahead because once his 25s Wind Wall is spent on your Q, everything lands for 20s.

edits.before: At 2+ items you win by reflecting his burst with W, rooting through the wall, and executing with Golden Eclipse.
edits.after: At 2+ items you win by reflecting his burst with W, rooting him post-wall, and executing with Golden Eclipse.

edits.before: Solar Snare (E) is a ground root that ignores Wind Wall (W), so you can lock Yasuo even when he raises his wall against your Radiant Volley (Q). Root him mid-Sweeping Blade (E) dash and chunk him before his flow shield regenerates; he has no sustain to trade back.
edits.after: Solar Snare (E) roots Yasuo mid-Sweeping Blade (E) dash — his 475-range kit has to walk through your slow zone to touch you. Root the approach, volley, and chunk him before his flow shield regenerates; he has no sustain to trade back. His wall can block the orb, so cast it off-angle.

edits.before: First item keeps you ahead: he wastes Wind Wall (W) on your Q, then eats a Solar Snare (E) root he can't wall through. Shove with Q and roam, since a Yasuo who blew his wall has no answer to your poke.
edits.after: First item keeps you ahead: bait Wind Wall (W) with Radiant Volley (Q) — 25s cooldown against your 10s — then land the Solar Snare (E) he can no longer block. Shove and roam; a walled-out Yasuo has no answer to your poke.

edits.before: Two items in you punish his all-in: W reflects his tornado and blunts his burst, E roots him through the wall, and Golden Eclipse (R) executes him the instant his flow shield breaks. Bait his Wind Wall with Q, then E-lock and delete him.
edits.after: Two items in you punish his all-in: W reflects his tornado and blunts his burst, E roots him once his wall is spent, and Golden Eclipse (R) executes him the instant his flow shield breaks. Bait his Wind Wall with Q, then E-lock and delete him.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 stay yours because Solar Snare (E) is a ground-targeted root that ignores Wind Wall entirely, so his signature defensive tool doesn't save him from your lockdown. Root his dash, chunk him while his flow shield is down, and hold Rebuttal (W) for the knockup he needs to ult.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 stay yours because Wind Wall (W) is a 25-second cooldown against your 10-second Q — bait it out, then root his Sweeping Blade (E) approach with Solar Snare. Chunk him while his flow shield is down, and hold Rebuttal (W) for the Steel Tempest tornado he needs to ult.

edits.before: With items you continue to punish his engage: W reflects his tornado and blunts his burst, E roots him through the wall, and Golden Eclipse (R) executes him once his shield breaks. Bait Wind Wall with a Q, then lock Solar Snare (E) and finish him before he can reset.
edits.after: With items you continue to punish his engage: W reflects his tornado and blunts his burst, Solar Snare locks him once his wall is spent, and Golden Eclipse (R) executes him when his shield breaks. Bait Wind Wall with a Q, then land E and finish him before he can reset.

edits.before: Root Yasuo with Solar Snare (E), which ignores Wind Wall (W)
edits.after: Root Yasuo's Sweeping Blade (E) approach with Solar Snare (E)

notes: CHART LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE: full says Yasuo wins all 7 stages (HARD 8/10), content and the packet say Mel wins all 7, WR is 48.46% — the layers already disagree on every row and neither blanket verdict is defensible from the kits, so I did not move any row; see questionsForUser. The 'Solar Snare ignores Wind Wall' claim (repeated across 8 content fields) contradicts the kit's projectile flag and Riot's 'fires a radiant orb forward' text, so it was removed everywhere; if the site owner has verified in-game that the root applies at the orb's ground zone despite the wall, revert those edits. Whether Rebuttal reflecting the Q3 tornado also cancels the knockup on Yasuo's side is asserted by existing text and plausible (it is a projectile) — left standing, listed unverified.
